title: The Morning Build for November 6, 2026: GPT-6 Cyber, Palo Alto Talks for Clutch, and Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash
intro: Today’s stories center on AI applied to security and infrastructure: OpenAI released a security-focused model that finds and exploits real vulnerabilities; Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to buy an AI-agent access security startup; Anthropics’ Claude Code raised a privacy bug on GitHub; Baidu open-sourced a 280B-parameter base model designed for long contexts; and a two-person lab published a $21K-trained video diffusion model and a plan for post-training.
meta_description: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber finds and exploits real bugs; Palo Alto in talks to buy Clutch for $500M; Baidu open-sources ERNIE 5.5 Flash base (280B params).

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber that finds, exploits, and suggests patches for real-world vulnerabilities
stories.what_happened: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber, a model trained to find vulnerabilities, produce working exploits, and propose fixes; in tests it found 81 previously unknown severe Firefox bugs and reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, producing 948 working exploits and reporting 304 critical findings to maintainers. OpenAI reports benchmark scores including 48.5% on ExploitGym and a 40.3% hit rate for web-app vuln discovery without source access, all from its system card and internal tests.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers should note a vendor-grade model now produces operational exploit proofs and patch suggestions at scale, with OpenAI reporting automated scout-and-analyst agents that scanned 5,034 kernel locations and cost $1.21M total compute for the Linux run. The model’s outputs and integration into reporting channels mean maintainers and defenders will need new workflows for triage, forensics, and verifying machine-generated fixes.
stories.outlook: OpenAI will expand access gradually from selected Daybreak Red customers to broader Daybreak tiers as it scales the program and says it plans to make the Daybreak for Frontline Defenders funding and a Daybreak Red subgroup available for critical-infrastructure testing.

stories.headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to acquire AI-agent security startup Clutch for about $500M
stories.what_happened: TechCrunch reports Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to buy Clutch Security for $500 million in cash plus milestone payouts; Clutch, founded three years ago, was last valued at $85 million and is approaching $10 million ARR, implying roughly a 50x ARR multiple if the deal completes.
stories.why_it_matters: For engineers and operators, the reported deal signals incumbent network-security vendors are acquiring technology that controls AI agents’ access to corporate systems, which could influence how agent access controls, identity checks, and policy enforcement integrate into existing firewall and CASB stacks.
stories.outlook: Completion of the acquisition or a formal Palo Alto announcement or regulatory filing will confirm the transaction and its integration plans, which TechCrunch frames as part of Palo Alto’s series of acquisitions this year.

stories.headline: Anthropic’s Claude Code reported to leak user email addresses in User-Agent headers; built-in privacy mod added in v2.1.317
stories.what_happened: A GitHub issue reports Claude Code sent the user’s personal email in the User-Agent header while performing web requests, exposing the address to third parties; the repository thread records a built-in privacy mod named cc-plugin-privacy was introduced in v2.1.317 and later to deterministically block this behavior and is enabled by default.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers embedding web-capable agents or running Claude Code locally should treat agent-origin headers as a potential PII leak vector and account for repository-level changes to the client; the vendor has added a default privacy plugin but the issue thread shows community concern and small-scale mitigations such as local hooks.
stories.outlook: Publication of the cc-plugin-privacy source or further commits to the Anthropic/Claude Code repository will show whether the built-in mod’s checks are fully auditable and complete the mitigation promised in the issue thread.

stories.headline: Baidu open-sources ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, a 280B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with long-context training
stories.what_happened: Baidu released ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base with 280 billion parameters and a MoE design that activates 14 billion parameters per input; the model was pre-trained on 33.5 trillion tokens with training context up to 128,000 tokens and weights are available on Hugging Face in FP8 and BF16. Baidu says a post-trained version will follow.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers building long-context systems or fine-tuning large foundation models get an open base with extreme context targets and MoE sparsity details; the availability of FP8 and BF16 weights enables cost-optimized deployments and research into scaling long-context inference and fine-tuning to reach the stated up-to-one-million-token capability.
stories.outlook: Baidu’s promised post-trained ERNIE 5.5 release will be the next milestone to evaluate how the base weights are adapted for downstream tasks and whether the one-million-token inference goal is supported in released checkpoints.

stories.headline: Two-person lab publishes Pyramid-JiT video diffusion model trained for about $21K and details a post-training plan
stories.what_happened: Linum published Field Notes on Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT), a pixel-space diffusion architecture trained over ~660M samples on 64 H100s, reporting convergence improvements and a pressure test run costing roughly $21,000; the authors describe architecture, training schedules, hardware (64× H100), and explicit limitations such as poor rendered-text handling and multi-entity scenes.
stories.why_it_matters: The post provides concrete training recipes, hardware counts, and optimizer and EMA parameters that engineers can reproduce or adapt for efficient video-model experiments; it also highlights the unresolved area of diffusion post-training and specific hyperparameters used in large-resolution transitions.
stories.outlook: Linum says it will publish more on its post-training stack and methods in the coming weeks, which will detail their Finite Difference Flow Optimization pipeline and human-in-the-loop post-training steps.

narration_script:
OpenAI published GPT-6 Cyber, a model trained to find vulnerabilities, build working exploits, and propose fixes. OpenAI reports the model found 81 previously unknown severe Firefox bugs and reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, producing 948 working exploits and reporting 304 critical findings. The company ran an automated scout-and-analyst agent pipeline that scanned about 5,034 kernel locations and says the kernel campaign cost $1.21 million in compute. OpenAI plans to expand access from selected Daybreak Red customers to broader Daybreak tiers and highlights funding for frontline defenders.

TechCrunch reports Palo Alto Networks is negotiating to acquire Clutch Security for about $500 million in cash plus milestones. Clutch is reported to be approaching $10 million ARR and was last valued at $85 million. The deal, if completed, would signal further consolidation of AI-agent access controls into incumbent security stacks; a formal announcement or regulatory filing will confirm the transaction.

A GitHub issue against Claude Code documents that the client sent a user’s personal email in the User-Agent header while performing web requests. The project added a built-in privacy mod called cc-plugin-privacy in v2.1.317 that is enabled by default to block this behavior, and the issue thread notes the maintainers plan to publish the mod source.

Baidu released ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base, an open foundation model with 280 billion parameters in a Mixture-of-Experts layout that activates 14 billion parameters per input. Baidu reports pre-training on 33.5 trillion tokens with training context up to 128,000 tokens and released FP8 and BF16 weights on Hugging Face; a post-trained version is planned to follow.

A two-person lab published Pyramid-JiT, a pixel-space diffusion video model trained in a cost envelope the authors report around $21,000. They detail training schedules, optimizer settings, EMA behavior, hardware (64 H100), and model limits such as an inability to generate rendered text; they say they will publish further work on their post-training stack in the coming weeks.

Those are the main updates for today. Expect OpenAI’s Daybreak access expansions and the Daybreak Red subgroup details, a formal notice or filing if Palo Alto completes the Clutch acquisition, publication of the cc-plugin-privacy source or repository commits for Claude Code, Baidu’s post-trained ERNIE 5.5 release, and Linum’s forthcoming post-training paper or notes in the next weeks.
